### 2026-10-22 – # Started  Working on the  MIDI pad!

**3.5h**

# Started  Working on the  MIDI pad!

## N.T: This devlog is from the work done on Monday 19/10/26.

## Journal log

So today I started working on the midi pad! I have a few design requirements in my mind. Here are all of them in descending order of priority:

1. USB C
2. RP2040 based.
3. 4x3 switch matrix using standard mechanical switches.
4. TFT display 1.8"
5. EC-11 rotary encoders
6. Debug and extra GPIO pin headers.

Eventually while wiring everything I ran out of GPIO pins that I could use.  This led to me finally needing to use a I2C I/O expander, I chose the [MCP23017x-x-SO I2C EXPANSION IC](https://www.ktron.in/product/mcp23017t-e-so-16-bit-i-o-expander).  I connected the rotary encoder pins A and B to this because timing isn't really as important for them compared to the keys which require the least latency as possible.This was
my choice due to a few reasons.

1. It doesn't require that many passives or decoupling capacitors compared to alternatives.
2. It is pretty easy to source.
3. Claude recommended it. This was cross examined by the datasheet.
4. It can be soldered by hand.

Anyway, let me show you my schematic

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/CNJdyyJ4I8fzZ0Pr2VdvErZElnDPPMWi/63d575f0571ec847c45802ae98eb03555744aee99453af31f1e8871ee93c99ac.png)

##  Schematic sanity checking

I followed though with Claude's advice and added external pull up resistors on the I2C communication lines namely, SCL and SDA. Then I had to assign footprints to all the components. Also i used a 100nf decoupling capacitor on the I/O expansion IC.

# PCB DESIGN!

## Includes work done on 22/10/26 and 23/10/26

I started the PCB layout and routing.

I had to change the pinout for the display module as i am using a more documented one now, the [Waveshare 128x160 General 1.8 Inch LCD Display Module](https://robu.in/product/waveshare-128x160-general-1-8-inch-lcd-display-module/).

I used a plugin to import the jlcpcb library footprint for this module.

Heres the new pin out

### 2026-10-24 – # PCB FINALIZED

**5h**

# PCB FINALIZED

## N.T: This journal isn't backdated! Reviewers might rejoice.

So, I finished the routing for then entire PCB, rather the routing process finished me. It was long and tedious and was a path filled with many a vias, but I finished it, just in the nick of time. Then came the DRC. [insert scared cat]

WELL you know what? it wasn't that bad, it might have been bad if i was new to PCB design, but i am not an amateur. Just a few unconnected ground pours and a few track clearance issues, which to be honest, wasn't all that hard to fix. Well now we are in the last few hours of the project

##  Whats next?

- FIRMWARE, this is a big one
- Repo making and writing the readme.md

About the case now, i wont be doing any cad for this week as I am tired of onshape from the past weeks project and want atleast one week off from CAD.
